title: Is the longest shared jump always the highest common factor?
description: The Jump Jackpot game is looked at again with treasures on thirty and fifty. A landing jump is shown to be a factor of each treasure number, so it is a common factor, and the longest one is the highest common factor. Keeko's doubt, a jump that is a multiple of both numbers, is tested on the number line.
teaching_notes: One idea: a jump lands on a number only if its size is a factor of that number, so the longest shared jump is the highest common factor. Watch for students who mix up factors, which are smaller, with multiples, which are larger.

source: Is the longest jump size for two treasure numbers always the
video_script.why: The child has found longest jumps by listing and now asks why the answer matches the highest common factor.
video_script.substitution: A landing jump is a factor of the treasure number, so a jump that lands on both is a common factor, and the longest one is the highest common factor.
video_script.anchor: A number line from zero with treasures on thirty and fifty.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the jump must be a multiple of both treasure numbers, so the longest jump is huge. A jump of 150 flies past 30 and 50 and lands on neither.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the longest jump is always the highest common factor.

final_answer.value: Yes: the longest jump is the HCF
final_answer.spoken: yes, the longest jump landing on both numbers is their highest common factor

names.Jia: places treasures on numbers in the Jump Jackpot game
names.Leeza: chooses a jump size in the Jump Jackpot game

maths_rules: A jump of size s from 0 lands on N exactly when N is a multiple of s, that is when s divides N.
So s is a factor of 30 and a factor of 50, a common factor of 30 and 50.
Common factors of 30 and 50: 1, 2, 5, 10; the longest jump is the largest, 10 = HCF.
The argument holds for any two numbers, so the answer is yes.
Slip: 150 is a multiple of 30 and of 50, but a jump of 150 from 0 lands first on 150, past both treasures.
video_script.design: One idea: landing means being a factor, so the longest shared jump is the highest common factor. Assumes the jump lists. Wrong idea: the jump is a multiple of both numbers. The number line stays all video.
